questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Italy, since I have Italian heritage and wanted to better my command of the Italian language. This I also did in Milan, although not to the extent I wanted. Furthermore, I accepted my exchange to Milan given the city's status as the economic capital of Italy.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Erasmus experience would not be possible in Milan without the Erasmus Student Network (ESN), since they facilitated the whole welcome week and made sure, that there were events for students to attend. Otherwise, Milan can be quite a difficult city for newcomers and expats.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. The University of Milan answer their mails, and I usually always received answer after a week. Otherwise, they continued to send out information to us students, although this sometimes wasn't completely clear cut.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I managed to get by on my own, as I speak an okay Italian. Otherwise, the ESN people were good guides for the rest.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Their info-mails should maybe be written in a more clear cut language to avoid ambiguity, but essentially it worked well.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found accommodation on AirBnB, and this was quite easy, when you are early out to look.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Follow the ESN-guys, enjoy the city - and look VERY early for housing, since it can be hard to find something close to semester-start.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Special system online. You register and then go to classes and confirm your attendance there. Later, the professors and the University confirm you registrations.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: University mail, online-guide and people on campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. Got all of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Quite simple. Don't sweat it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNIMI is still in the proces of developing some of their English-language classes. The level was okay, though, and the material matched the ECTS.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Many different levels. It all depends on the course and the professor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit more traditional, compared to UCPH. Much more auditorium lectures, and less seminar dicussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
M&A: The Contract
European Monetary and Economic Law
Negotiation, Mediation and Sustainable Conflict Resolution
Smart Cities, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation Law
Access to Justice in a Multilevel Constitutional System

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would really recommend M&A: The Contract, since Prof. Toffoletto is incredibly good. The classes were interesting and engaging.
Furthermore, European Monetary and Economic Law was really interesting, and although the course had a more traditional teaching method, the content of the course inspires reflection.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't do activities at the host institution. Things were planned though ESN La Statale

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't do activities at the host institution. Things were planned though ESN La Statale

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Verona or Como/Lecco - or go the other cities around. It's really nice to go mountain walking around the Como Lake. Sicily is also worth a visit! and in December, there is the Fiera, meaning the Fair, where all the food of Italy and the world is up for tasting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy, although I am used to the South of Italy, where people are more warm and open.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Push it, force it, get in there. Don't be desperate, but try!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any, except that Professors are of higher societal standing in Italy, and you address them and other professions by title, not by name.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Language and Food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Meet the ESN-people, travel out of Milan to the whole of the North with train and meet locals, hard as it can be in Milan.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember that the metro-card is 22€ per month for students in the whole urban area.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Finally getting local friends towards the end of my stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It is quite hard integrating into Milan, as the city is quite busy. People are a bit cold. So finding friends from the local area might be tough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
